name: Albilad Capital
legal_name: Albilad Investment Company (a Saudi Closed Joint Stock Company), trading as Albilad Capital
founded: 2007 (registered as a limited liability company 20 Nov 2007, CR 1010240489; CMA letter 2-38-2007 dated 22 Jul 2007; CMA licence 08100-37 dated 14 Aug 2007). Converted to a closed joint stock company on 10 Jul 2017. Forbes Middle East and company press releases say 'established in 2008'.
ownership_summary: 100% owned by Bank Albilad. Share capital SAR 500m (raised from SAR 200m during 2024). Paid SAR 150m of dividends to the parent in 2024.
government_link: Indirect at most: PIF was the anchor investor in the Albilad MSCI Saudi Equity ETF (Oct 2025), but holds no stake in the company. The parent has no government shareholder above 5% (see sa-albilad).
group_structure: 100% subsidiary of Bank Albilad (sa-albilad), consolidated by the parent and reported inside its 'Investment banking and brokerage' segment (FY2025 operating income SAR 433.0m; the segment was within SAR 1m of Albilad Capital's own FY2024 operating income of SAR 404.0m). Never add this record's figures to sa-albilad. The parent AR calls Albilad Capital 'the Bank's investments and capital-markets arm, critical to wealth management, fund performance, and corporate finance execution'. Its only external financing is two short-term SAR 50m murabaha facilities from Saudi National Bank (AR 2025).
footprint: Saudi Arabia, head office in Riyadh. The sources opened name no branch network. International trading is offered through the Albilad Global app; Albilad Capital ETFs are listed on the Saudi Exchange and the firm cites a 52% share of GCC ETF market capitalisation (Oct 2025).
customer_segments: Retail and affluent investors (public funds from SAR 5,000, ETFs, brokerage), discretionary portfolio clients, institutions and government (sukuk primary dealer, IPO and sukuk mandates), developers and real estate sponsors (fund structuring), foreign investors via ETFs.
business_lines: FY2024 audited operating income SAR 404.0m: asset management SAR 146.1m, securities services (custody) SAR 107.0m, brokerage net SAR 92.3m, special commission (margin lending) SAR 38.4m, advisory SAR 15.0m. Lines: 7 listed ETFs (Saudi equity, US equity and tech, Hong Kong China, gold, sovereign sukuk), public mutual funds (12 listed), discretionary portfolio management, real estate and hospitality funds, brokerage (Saudi and international, online Murabaha margin, single stock options), investment banking (IPO and sukuk mandates), securities custody, research (monthly market reports).

capabilities.wealth_summary: Albilad Capital is Bank Albilad's licensed investment arm and the product engine behind the bank's investment offer. It manages a large ETF franchise (7 ETFs; about SAR 6bn and 64% of Saudi ETF market cap in Oct 2025), real estate funds (assets managed approaching SAR 21bn in Nov 2025), 12 listed public mutual funds, and discretionary portfolios, and offers Saudi and international brokerage with online Murabaha margin and single stock options. Forbes Middle East cites USD 10.35bn of AUM for 2025 (unverified). FY2024 operating income was SAR 404m (asset management SAR 146m, custody SAR 107m, brokerage SAR 92m); the parent's segment data suggest SAR 433m in FY2025 and a 19% fall in H1 2026. Product strategy leans on third-party partners: KraneShares (2023 MoU), CSOP (Hong Kong China ETF), State Street (Nov 2025 securities-services agreement) and Asset Management One (Dec 2025 MoU for a Japan equity ETF due by end-2026). The distribution side is digital: 76% of turnover through web and mobile, a new Albilad-Capital Saudi trading app (2026), Albilad Global apps for international markets, and distribution through the Madkhol app (Jan 2026). No wealth management or advisory page, model portfolios or structured products were found.

private_banking.detail: No private banking unit at Albilad Capital; Private Banking is run by the parent bank (see sa-albilad). The asset management page lists discretionary portfolios with no minimum.

asset_management.detail: 7 ETFs (sovereign sukuk 9403, MSCI US Equity, Gold, MSCI US Tech, MSCI Saudi Growth, CSOP MSCI Hong Kong China, MSCI Saudi Equity), about SAR 6bn ETF AUM and 64% Saudi ETF market cap (Oct 2025); 12 listed public mutual funds (Saudi Equity Income, GCC Equity Income, SAR Murabaha, Kuwait Equity, Diversified SAR, Fund of REIT, Ensan Endowment, Multi-Assets Balanced, Pure Saudi Equity, Freestyle Saudi Equity, Sukuk, King Faisal University Endowment); real estate and hospitality funds (Makkah Vision, Qurtubah Square, Hittin, Albilad Real Estate Fund II, Albilad Hospitality Fund I). Minimum subscription SAR 5,000 on the Saudi Equity Income Fund. Approved as market maker for three ETFs from 21 Sep 2026.

brokerage.detail: Local and international trading, online Murabaha, trading packages, single stock options, public subscription (IPO) services; brokerage income SAR 92.3m net in FY2024; margin lending receivable SAR 354.7m at end-2024; 76% of turnover via web and mobile in 2025. Apps: Albilad-Capital (Saudi equities, funds, ETFs, IPOs, margin; 2026), Albilad Tadawul (older Saudi app) and Albilad Global / Global Lite (Shariah-compliant stocks, ETFs and options on international markets). Commissions not published on the page opened.

digital_investing.detail: New 'Albilad-Capital' app (App Store, copyright 2026; account opening, Saudi equities, mutual funds and ETFs, IPO subscription, margin, P&L and average cost reports). Older 'Albilad Tadawul' app (v3.0.4, June 2024, 2.1 stars from 68 ratings). 'Albilad Global' and 'Global Lite' for international markets. AR 2025 adds conditional orders, biometric login, buying-power calculator and a 'Super App' in beta with streamlined mobile onboarding and KYC. Funds are also offered inside the Madkhol app (announced Jan 2026).

advisory.detail: CMA licence covers advising and FY2024 income included SAR 15.0m of advisory fees (investment banking side). No retail or wealth advisory service is described on the pages opened.

discretionary.detail: Discretionary Portfolio Management is listed on the asset management page; no minimum, mandate types or fee published; DPM AUM not disclosed.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisor or model portfolio product found on the website, in the App Store listings or in AR 2025. Multi-Assets Balanced Fund is the closest risk-profiled option.

funds_platform.detail: Own funds and ETFs only. No third-party fund shelf found; third-party involvement is as ETF sub-advisers or index providers (CSOP, MSCI, Ideal Ratings) and distribution partner Madkhol.

structured_products.detail: No structured products on the product pages opened (asset management, brokerage).

private_markets.detail: Real estate assets managed approaching SAR 21bn (CEO, Nov 2025): Makkah Vision Real Estate Fund (about SAR 11bn, with Thakher and the Royal Commission for Makkah as sponsor; launched May 2025), Albilad Real Estate Fund II (SAR 4.4bn, Qurtubah, Riyadh), Albilad Hospitality Fund I (Mövenpick Riyadh, about SAR 1bn), Albilad Tourism Fund with the Tourism Development Fund (Rixos Murjana), and a Tilal MoU for a SAR 1.2bn Al Khobar project.

islamic_wealth.detail: Funds and ETFs are described as complying with Albilad Capital's Shariah Committee: sovereign sukuk ETF, Shariah-screened MSCI ETFs, Murabaha and sukuk funds, Shariah-compliant global stocks, ETFs and options in Albilad Global, planned Shariah-compliant Japan equity ETF. Whether the whole firm is Shariah-only is not stated (model left 'Not applicable').

discrepancies.detail: The company's board CVs name Ihsan Bafakih Chairman (since April 2023) and Abdulaziz AlOnaizan Vice Chairman; the parent's board page (Oct 2026) says AlOnaizan is 'Chairman of Albilad Capital'. An executive directory seen in search results still lists Bafakih as Chairman (updated 3 Jun 2026). The CVs are undated (Dec 2023 file metadata); AlOnaizan became bank Chairman on 1 Jun 2026.
discrepancies.resolution: Both recorded with role_status 'Conflicting sources'. Unresolved; check the Albilad Capital board page or a Tadawul/CMA filing.

discrepancies.detail: Oct 2025 release: 64% of Saudi ETF market cap and 52% of GCC. Parent AR 2025: above 70% local and about 53% regional. An undated 2024 release: 70% of Saudi ETFs and 60% of ETF unit holders.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded the dated Oct 2025 release (64%) as the metric and the others in notes. Different measures or dates.

discrepancies.detail: Forbes ME gives USD 10.35bn (2025). Company statements give real estate approaching SAR 21bn (about USD 5.6bn) and ETFs about SAR 6bn (about USD 1.6bn). State Street's release cites over USD 50bn in assets under custody and/or administration (a different measure). No company-published total AUM.
discrepancies.resolution: Forbes AUM recorded as 'Requires verification'; component figures and AUA recorded separately.

discrepancies.detail: Registered 20 Nov 2007 (FS); CMA licence date 14 Aug 2007; releases and Forbes say 2008.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the FS date for registration and noted 2008 as the commonly stated year. Minor.

discrepancies.detail: A fund board biography calls the CEO 'Country Chief Financial Officer' with 15+ years in markets, which does not match his CEO role elsewhere (likely a drafting error in the fund report).
discrepancies.resolution: Used press releases and Forbes ME for the title. Minor.

open_items: No FY2025 or interim standalone financial statements found on albilad-capital.com (FY2024 is the latest; a guessed FY2025 URL returned 404). Metrics are FY2024. FY2025 and H1 2026 income are shown only as the parent's segment proxy. Re-check the website's financial reports and the parent's Q3 2026 statements in late Oct 2026.

No company-published total AUM, discretionary AUM, client numbers, investing users or headcount found. Forbes USD 10.35bn is unverified; State Street's USD 50bn+ is assets under custody and/or administration, not AUM.

The company website is a thin landing page: About, management, board, wealth management and financial-reports pages were not found, so people come from fund reports, board CVs, press releases, LinkedIn search results and an executive directory. Only the CEO, Chairman and board member Al-Suhaimi have documentary support; the CIO, COO and Head of Brokerage are 'Requires verification'.
Chairman of Albilad Capital: conflicting evidence (see discrepancies). Whether the AlOnaizan board CV is current is unknown.

Technology vendors for the Saudi trading app, Albilad Tadawul (DirectFN copyright line) and Albilad Global (IB Exchange Corp. copyright line) are inferred from App Store listings only; the new Albilad-Capital app lists no vendor.
